chapter: New York, Philadelphia and Harlem nightlife
title: Earning a hundred dollars a day in New York in 1937-38
summary: He marvels at making a hundred dollars for three hours' recording work, compared with the trumpet teacher and Ella B. Moore.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: For example, can you imagine me coming to New York City, being in the same town with Duke Ellington, Count Basie, Liberate or whoever in the hell was great...and Vincent Lopez and

going down to a company...the same company that Guy Lombardo was, you know what I mean, the King...and Bing Crosby...the first check I ever saw for a million dollars, you know what I mean, Bing had it, and all that. Can you imagine Sammy Price...again, I go back to that man with the trumpet, and that woman and Ella B. Moore, and then Kansas City with Ellis Burden and all the way up the line. Can you imagine my being in New York City in 1937 or early '38 making a hundred dollars for a day's work! Three hours!
